correctness.rationale: For w=2r+1, k=w−2q, compare adjacent windows as labeled multisets, counting clamped copies separately. The shared observations with shared ranks q+1 through w−q−1 necessarily survive either insertion. Thus a step direction changes the retained binary-tag count by at most one across an edge. For a cut just before j, only edge indices j−r−1 through j+r−1 can contribute, intersected with the path. Step decomposition and segment integration over ordering chambers, with continuity at ties, give min(w,n−1)/k. For n=w+1, use the even values followed by odd values and perturb the right half positively by ε<1. At left center i the rank of 2j−1 is r+2j−i. The admissible j are the intersection of [1,i] with the integer interval [ceil((i+2−t)/2),floor((i+t)/2)], t=r−q+1. This gives the reported counts and unit successive changes. Reflected counts are k minus the original counts and the two central counts differ by one since the middle k consecutive integers have odd count (k±1)/2. Appending the last value and its step tag preserves the original outputs and denominator. This proves attainment and strict inequality on shorter paths including the mean and median endpoints.
residual_risks: The shorter-length bound need not be sharp; no exact short-path classification is certified.

value.rationale: Gives the exact perturbation amplification uniformly across the standard robustness continuum from moving mean to median. The overlap lemma explains why averaging adjacent ranks is much better than adding rank-filter norms, while the parity construction and first attainable length identify when the worst amplification is physically possible on a finite path.
residual_risks: The result is for unweighted clamped paths, not a bound on arbitrary boundary conventions or a claim of historical priority.
